_about: Registry marker name -> candidate KRONOS marker_metadata.csv marker_name values (UPPERCASE), in priority order.
Written 2026-09-05 BEFORE marker_metadata.csv could be read (MahmoodLab/KRONOS is gated; access awaiting review), from
the naming style the KRONOS tutorial's own manual map uses ('PD-1' -> 'PD1', 'BCL-2' -> 'BCL2', 'GRANZYME B' -> 'GZMB',
1. the uppercased registry name; 2. the 'aliases' list (the marker's OWN identity under other spellings);
3. a punctuation-free comparison of 1-2 against every metadata name;
4. the 'fallbacks' list (a biologically similar family marker, the tutorial's 'COLLAGEN 4' -> 'COLLAGEN' idiom),
applied only after every marker has had its pass at 1-3 so a family name is never taken from the marker it names;
5. otherwise an unused ODD marker_id adjacent to the metadata marker with the highest name similarity (the
tutorial's suggestion rule; odd ids are the ones KRONOS reserves for markers absent from pretraining) with
mean/std computed from this donor's frame window planes on the 0-1 scale.
A metadata id is never given to two channels; the first marker (ctx.markers order) keeps it and the next one moves
down its list. Every assignment and the step that produced it is recorded in the run record and the sidecar JSON.
Editing this table after a result has been seen is a configuration change and therefore a new arm name.
